picker_prompt: Who are you? Every verdict is saved under this name.
picker_create_label: Not in the list? Add yourself
picker_create_hint: Letters, digits, space, dot, dash and underscore, up to 64 characters.
list_empty_mine: No batches for you: none in work, none available.
lock_mine: You hold this batch; nobody else can mark it. It finishes by itself on your last verdict.
lock_available: This batch is free. Take it to record verdicts; while you hold it, nobody else can mark it.
lock_locked: {name} holds this batch. You can only look for now.
lock_done: You finished this batch. You can still change your verdicts.
lock_closed: This batch is not for you: it has its reviews, or you may not take it. You can only look.
item_beyond_video_warn: The item starts after the end of the video ({seconds} s), the player will open it from the start. Judge by the text, plus the "Subtitle track ≠ video" flag.
item_no_player: No player link for this item.
current_legacy_wrong_text: (legacy "Wrong text": re-decide with the track flag)
flags_hint: A flag is a separate fact about the video, not a verdict. Tick it when it is true for this video; a verdict by the text is needed either way.
track_flag: Subtitle track ≠ video (text or timing off; whole video)
rules_who_paid_html: Sponsor — an outside party paid for this piece. Self-promotion — the speaker promotes themselves: subscribe, like, comment, own products, channels, events, client work. The test is who paid, not how long or how annoying it is.
rules_call_to_action_html: A call to action woven into the content ("write in the comments which…") is still self-promotion; say in the comment that you would not skip it. Whether to skip is decided by thresholds in code, not here.
rules_not_ad_html: Not an ad — the text is neither. Unclear — only when the text itself does not let you decide.
rules_track_html: Judge the verdict by the text. The player disagrees (other words, the same words shifted, a video shorter than the item that opens from the start)? Still decide by the text and tick Subtitle track ≠ video as well: it marks the whole video, not this item. Never pick "Unclear" because of the player.
signals_no_videos: no video rows for this native_id
signals_no_markups: No live markups in the window.
signals_no_segments: No calculated segments in the window.
auto_advance: After saving, open the next item
onb_summary: How to work here — read this once
onb_what_html:
Our service helps the video platform viewers skip ads in videos. A program reads the subtitles of videos and looks for pieces that look like ads. Sometimes it gets them wrong.

You check these pieces. One piece is an item: a short stretch of subtitles (the large text with the quote mark). Your job is to say what this text is. Items are grouped into batches.

Your answers show us how well the program works. So decide on your own and honestly. The "Proposed as:" line is the program's guess, not the right answer. The "Signals" block at the bottom is background: what viewers marked near this place. You can decide without it.
onb_workflow_html:
1. Your name is shown at the top ("Reviewer: …"). Every verdict is saved under it, so always come in under the same name.
  2. In the batch list, open a batch from the "Available" section.
  3. Press "Take it". The batch is now yours: while you hold it, nobody else can mark it. Until you take the batch, the verdict buttons do not work.
  4. On each item, read the text, watch the video if needed, pick a verdict and press "Save ⏎". The next item opens right away.
  5. When you save the last item, the batch finishes by itself and moves to the "Done" section.
  • Need a break? You do not have to press anything. The batch stays in the "In work" section; continue where you stopped.
  • Not going to finish? Press "Give up". Your verdicts are kept, and someone else can take the batch.
  • Made a mistake? Go back to the item with the ◀ button at the top, pick another verdict and save again. This also works after the batch is done.
  • A batch "locked by" another person can only be viewed. The "Give up" button on it takes the batch away from that person. Press it only if they agree or have disappeared: ask in the shared chat first.
  • If someone else has already checked an item, their answer is shown in the "Current verdict:" block. Still decide on your own.
onb_verdicts_html:
The main question: who paid for this text? It does not matter whether the piece is long or short, annoying or not.

  • Sponsor — an outside party paid: a bank, a shop, a service, another channel. Example: "This episode is supported by bank N. Get the card with the link in the description."
  • Self-promotion — the author promotes themselves: asks you to subscribe, like or comment; talks about their own products, channels, courses, concerts. Example: "Subscribe to the channel and hit the bell so you don't miss new videos."
  • Not an ad — neither, a normal part of the video. Example: "Now we take the lid off and look inside."
  • Unclear — only when the text itself does not let you decide. Example: "…and the link, as always, is in the description" — the piece does not tell whose link it is: a sponsor's or the author's own. Write in the comment what was missing.

A call to action inside the story itself ("write in the comments which option you like more") is Self-promotion too. If you would not skip something like this, say so in the comment.
onb_track_html:
Sometimes the subtitles do not match the video: the player has other words, or the same words but earlier or later, or the video is shorter than the item's time and the player opens it from the start. One rule:

  1. Judge the verdict by the subtitle text, as if there were no player. Never pick "Unclear" because of the player: it is only for a text that does not decide by itself.
  2. Additionally tick Subtitle track ≠ video (key {flag}). It tells us the times of this video cannot be trusted; it does not replace the verdict.
  • The tick is about the whole video, not one item. It is saved together with the verdict, by the "Save ⏎" button.
  • On other items of the same video the tick is already set, and you can see who set it. If it is set by mistake, untick it and save.
  • When we know the video length and the item starts after its end, a yellow warning shows above the text: the player will show nothing useful there, which is expected.
onb_player_html:
• The "Open in player ↗" link (key {player}) opens the video on the video platform in a new tab, right at the needed place.
  • When you move to another item (the ◀ / ▶ buttons, "first open", keys {next} / {prev}, or after "Save ⏎"), the page prepares the video in advance. The new item opens in a new tab, and the tab you were in becomes the player for that item. It is usually the next tab to the left. While you read the text, the video is already loading.
  • After a save, the video tab of the previous item closes by itself.
  • If you clear the "After saving, open the next item" box at the bottom of the page, a save keeps you on the same item and the video tab stays open. The browser remembers the choice.
  • Start your work from the batch list and open the batch from there. Otherwise the browser will not let the page close old video tabs, and you will have to close them yourself.
  • If the browser says it blocked a pop-up, allow pop-ups for this site. Without that, the page just moves to the next item and does not prepare the video.
onb_timing_html:
• Times are written as in the player: 1:05 is 1 minute 5 seconds, 1:02:30 is 1 hour 2 minutes 30 seconds.
  • The player starts 2 seconds before the piece on purpose, so you hear its beginning. So the text you need does not start right away. This is not a shift: do not tick "Subtitle track ≠ video" because of it.
  • An item's time can exceed the video length: the subtitles come from another, longer version of the video. Then the player opens it from the start (or the end). This is not a page error: judge by the text and tick "Subtitle track ≠ video".
onb_hotkeys_html: You can do everything from the keyboard, no mouse needed. The keys also work with a Russian keyboard layout. While you type a comment, the other keys do not work: press Esc to leave the box.
onb_comments_html:
• A comment is optional. Write one when you are unsure: briefly, why you chose this verdict.
  • Questions, bugs on the page and ideas go to the shared chat.
js_close_by_hand: Close the previous video tab by hand: the browser lets this page close only tabs it opened (start from the batch list).
js_read_only: You cannot record verdicts here right now: see the box at the top of the page.
js_force_confirm: {name} holds this batch. Release it? The verdicts of {name} stay.
conflict_done: You have already finished this batch.
conflict_closed: This batch is closed to you.
